advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Exclude container-criterion (G3/G4) cases that carry no inline `children` from eligible_cases, since run_case always raises on them, rather than admitting them and relying on errored-pair dropping.
evidence: solver_arm resolves G3 via `if eval_solver._criterion_id(solver_id, repo_root) is not None: return "criterion"` (provider_parity.py:151-152), so a container criterion is admitted by eligible_cases (`if solver_arm(solver_id, repo_root) is None: continue`, provider_parity.py:171)

eval_solver.py:110-116: `if cid in CONTAINER_CRITERIA:` ... `if not isinstance(children, list) or not children: raise ValueError(f"container criterion {cid!r} needs a non-empty `children` list ...")` — a pooled eval fixture case carries no inline `children`, so run_case raises

Ticket 0d76 live-run comment: 'plan-review-container's G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar and G3-FP-covered-by-named-consumer-rebar raised ValueError ... on BOTH arms at ALL 3 epochs, before any model call ... They are now excluded ... by `_runnable`' — i.e. this commit does not yet exclude them

The module docstring claims eligibility means the solver id 'RESOLVES to a non-agentic run_case arm' (provider_parity.py, header) — true of the arm dispatch but the arm then raises, so the guarantee the docstring implies (a runnable verdict) does not hold for container criteria
advisory.finding: The corpus selector admits container G3 criterion cases (e.g. the plan's own worked example G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar) whose run_case arm always raises: solver_arm() resolves a G3 case to the 'criterion' arm, but _run_criterion_case raises ValueError for a container criterion with no inline `children` payload, so these cases error on BOTH arms at EVERY epoch and are dropped — billable case-runs that can never produce a verdict.
scenarios: Any live run whose pooled corpus includes a plan-review-container spec: 2 gold cases x epochs x 2 arms x 2 slots error before any model call and are silently dropped, lowering n_gold toward the gold floor
advisory.suggested_fix: In solver_arm/eligible_cases, treat a container criterion id without a usable `children` payload as ineligible (return None), so it is filtered out before spend rather than erroring on both arms.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Align usage_model_tally with the real REBAR_USAGE_LOG format: filter on the row `outcome` field (OUTCOME_OK) or a non-zero input_tokens, not `input_tokens is not None`, and update the test fixture to use the actual sink shape (int input_tokens + outcome key).
evidence: Guard: `if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("model") and row.get("input_tokens") is not None:` (provider_parity.py:413), documented as 'only rows carrying a non-null input_tokens count as a model call, so failure rows ... cannot inflate the tally' (provider_parity.py:402-403)

usage_log.record always writes the field as an int: `for field in _FIELDS: row[field] = int(usage.get(field, 0) or 0)` (usage_log.py:311-312) — never null, and _FIELDS includes 'input_tokens' (usage_log.py:32)

record_failure(...) calls record(..., outcome=OUTCOME_FAILED) (usage_log.py:360-370), so a failed call's row carries input_tokens as an int (0 or the burned count), which passes the `is not None` guard

The test fixture encodes a failure row as `{"model": "anthropic:claude-opus-4-8", "input_tokens": None}` (test_provider_parity.py:240) — a shape the real sink never emits, so the test does not exercise the actual failure-row format
advisory.finding: usage_model_tally's `input_tokens is not None` guard does not exclude failure rows as its docstring claims: the real REBAR_USAGE_LOG writer (usage_log.record) always writes input_tokens as an int (0 for OUTCOME_FAILED rows), never null, so a failed non-Bedrock call would still be counted by non_bedrock_calls.
scenarios: A v2 arm that made a failed non-Bedrock call (input_tokens written as an int) — non_bedrock_calls would still surface it correctly, but a failure row the docstring promises to exclude is in fact counted; conversely a real failure row is never excluded as documented
advisory.suggested_fix: Reuse rebar.llm.usage_log's own reader / row shape, and gate on `row.get("outcome") == usage_log.OUTCOME_OK` (or `input_tokens > 0`) rather than `is not None`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide the policy for partially-errored items (e.g. require a minimum surviving-epoch count, or mark the item errored/dropped when a threshold of epochs raised) rather than silently taking a reduced-quorum majority.
evidence: Only a total wipeout marks the record errored: `if decisions:` builds a valid record from `majority_decision(decisions)`, else the errored branch runs (provider_parity.py:276-294)
Raised epochs increment out.errors but do not append to `decisions` (provider_parity.py:265-270), so a 2-of-3-failed item yields a single-vote 'majority'

Only SAMPLING_PARAMETER/AUTH_VALIDATION counts invalidate the slot (`_INVALIDATING = (SAMPLING_PARAMETER, AUTH_VALIDATION)`, provider_parity.py); a GENERIC partial failure neither invalidates nor is reflected in the scored record
advisory.finding: In run_arm, an item where only SOME epochs raise still produces a valid=True majority record computed over the surviving epochs only, while the raised epochs are counted into out.errors; the item is not marked errored, so its majority is silently taken over fewer than N epochs and non-invalidating (GENERIC) failures reduce majority robustness without any signal in the scored record.
scenarios: One arm intermittently throttles (GENERIC) on 2 of 3 epochs of a gold item: its recorded decision is a single-epoch verdict compared against the other arm's 3-epoch majority, which can manufacture a decision flip driven by noise rather than model behavior

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a solver returns disagreeing decisions across epochs for one item (e.g. 2 block / 1 advisory) and assert the item's recorded decision is the majority (and the block-cautious tie-break).
evidence: _solver returns a fixed decision per item: `decision = item.label` then `if item.case_id in flip: decision = ...` — no per-epoch variation (tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py:56-63)
run_arm reduces epochs via majority: `decision=majority_decision(decisions)` (src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py, run_arm)
majority_decision breaks ties toward `block` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py:127-136) — an untested tie-break contract
ABSENCE: no test drives a solver that returns different decisions across the 3 epochs of one item (e.g. 2 block / 1 advisory) to prove the majority is taken
advisory.finding: The epoch-majority reduction (run_arm -> majority_decision) is never exercised with per-epoch disagreement, so a regression in the aggregation cannot be caught. Every test solver (_solver) returns the same decision for all epochs of a given item, so majority_decision always receives a uniform list; a bug that returned the first or last epoch's decision instead of the majority would pass all current tests.
scenarios: A refactor of the epoch loop that keeps the last epoch instead of the majority
A regression in majority_decision's block-cautious tie-break
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend _solver to accept a per-epoch decision sequence (or a call counter) so one item can yield 2 block / 1 advisory across 3 epochs, then assert the ItemRecord decision is `block`; add a 1-block/1-advisory tie case asserting `block`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests for main(): assert `--dry-run` returns 0 and emits corpus_digest/n_items, and (via an injected/monkeypatched run_slot) assert the exit code is 1 for an unmeasured-only or invalid slot and 0 for an all-passing measured run.
evidence: `return 0 if measured and all(b["passed"] and not b["invalid"] for b in measured) else 1` (src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:562)
--dry-run prints corpus_digest/n_items and returns 0 with no model call (src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:528-542)
ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py calls pp.main(...) — the only occurrences of the module in tests are imports and the workflow grep (search: provider_parity)
advisory.finding: main() — the operator CLI entrypoint — and its exit-code contract are untested, though the --dry-run and exit-code paths are fully offline (no model call). main returns 0 only if `measured and all(b['passed'] and not b['invalid'])`; an all-slots-unmeasured run must return 1, and an invalid slot must return 1, but nothing exercises these.
scenarios: A change that makes main return 0 when no slot was measured
A change to --dry-run output shape or --limit truncation
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch pp.run_slot to return controlled blocks and assert main(['--slot','standard']) returns 1 for invalid/unmeasured and 0 for passing; separately assert main(['--dry-run']) == 0 and parses stdout JSON.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that pp.unmeasured_slot(slot, refusal) yields measured=False with the refusal quoted, and that such a block is not treated as a pass by the exit-code/recheck path.
evidence: `unmeasured_slot` listed in __all__ (src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py __all__)
docstring: 'Explicitly NOT a pass: the slot stays an open question' (unmeasured_slot)
ABSENCE: no reference to unmeasured_slot in tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py
advisory.finding: unmeasured_slot() is exported in __all__ but has no test, and the contract that an unmeasured slot is 'explicitly NOT a pass' is unverified anywhere.
scenarios: A refactor that lets an unmeasured slot lack a refusal or be treated as passing
